All other end uses are unaffected. The envelope upgrade reduced heat loss from the dwelling, which led to a slight increase in hot water energy consumption. In this example, the water heater is in an unheated basement. By preventing heat loss during winter and retaining cool air during summer, the upgrade improves overall thermal efficiency. However, because the unit is heating-dominated, the reduction in heat loss during winter is more significant than the benefit of retaining cool air in summer. As a result, less ambient heat is released into the unheated basement, causing the water heater to work harder and use slightly more energy to maintain the desired water temperature. The comprehensive envelope upgrade package reduces the dwelling unit’s annual total energy use from 165 MBtu to 95 MBtu, a 42% reduction. In contrast, air sealing, drill-and-fill wall insulation, duct sealing and insulation, and attic floor insulation individually reduced energy consumption by 18%, 18%, 8%, and 1%, respectively. This demonstrates that the full envelope package maximizes energy efficiency, highlighting the synergistic benefits of combining all four measures. Figure 1. Annual site energy consumption before and after envelope upgrades Figure 2 further breaks down the annual site energy savings for the dwelling unit, showing the impact of each individual measure and the combined effect of the full envelope upgrade package. Advanced air sealing provides the largest savings at 30.2 MBtu, followed by drill-and-fill wall insulation (30.0 MBtu), and duct sealing and insulation (12.8 MBtu). Attic floor insulation alone contributes a modest 2.4 MBtu. When all measures are implemented together, the total savings reach 69.1 MBtu, which is slightly lower than the sum of the individual impacts.
